non_blocking.suggestion: `Plugin.spec.configSchema` is itself a JSON Schema and can legitimately be recursive (the draft 2020-12 meta-schema is). Under "Lowering inlines `$ref` (recursion fails generation)", that would fail the Plugin CRD and break "one CRD per kind, all ten" and the Coverage driver. State that `Plugin.spec.configSchema` and Policy `config` lower to `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true` and are checked only in Ruralz Control, so recursion never reaches the generator.

The leader's own status writes, and server-set fields such as `resourceVersion` and `managedFields`, raise watch events. State that events which leave the translated object set unchanged neither restart the debounce window nor start a build. Also state that an assembly whose digest equals the namespace's last recorded object-set digest records nothing and starts no Rollout, and that conditions are written only when they change. Without these rules, each condition update during a canary bake re-runs the full pipeline.

"a debounce window, or after a maximum delay (both target values)" gives no numbers. Add numeric values tagged (target), or name the Open question that will fix them, so that the kind test asserting "exactly one Revision" has a concrete apply window to exercise.

"Server-set `metadata` and `status` are dropped" leaves user-set `metadata.namespace`, `finalizers` and `ownerReferences` in the Bundle. But the Configuration model's envelope accepts only `name`, `labels` and `annotations`, and it rejects `metadata.namespace`. Say instead that metadata other than name, labels and annotations is dropped (or rejected with a named RZ-CFG code), so an object another controller touched does not surface as RZ-CFG-006.

Control plane and GitOps says of the CRD source that "every Kubernetes user who changed the set is an author". Watch events carry no userInfo, though, and `managedFields` records only field-manager names, while this ADR's admission is structural schema plus CEL only. Add a Proposed amendment: per-user attribution needs a validating admission webhook or the Kubernetes audit log; otherwise the audit records managers only.

Add the list lowering. `x-ruralz-list` `map`/`orderedMap` become `x-kubernetes-list-type: map` with `x-kubernetes-list-map-keys: [name]`, `set` becomes `set`, and `atomic` becomes `atomic`, so that server-side apply merges by key as the Configuration model promises. Note that a server-side-apply merge of an `orderedMap` may not preserve authored order, and order is inside the digest.

The third Good bullet lists real degradations: frozen EndpointSlice discovery and secret refresh, and restarted Nodes that stay not ready. Move that clause into a Bad bullet so the balance reads honestly, and keep the P9 point as the Good.

The owning document's RBAC row grants `ruralz-control` only "cluster-scoped CRD status updates". Writing `Accepted`, `ResolvedRefs` and `Programmed` on namespaced objects needs `update` or `patch` on `<kind>/status` in bound namespaces. Record a Proposed amendment for the Deployment topologies RBAC row.

Once a second version is served (Planned (M3)), objects the webhook down-converts carry `ruralz.io/conversion-data`, a reserved prefix, and annotations are inside the digest. State that the translation handles that annotation in the same way whichever version it reads, so the choice of served version cannot change a namespace's digest.
